data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Thalassina refers to a sea goddess. This name is rooted in the Greek word 'thalassa' meaning 'sea'. As a Christian name, it represents the divine power and protection of the sea. The name Thalassina carries the meaning “Sea Goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Thalassina usually hope their child will grow to embody sea goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: Thalassina as a Christian name holds deep spiritual significance as it reminds us of God's control and care over the natural world and His people. It serves as a reminder of the comforting presence of God in times of turmoil and uncertainty, and the divine protection offered to us as His beloved children. The name Thalassina encourages us to trust in the divine providence and power of God, and to find peace and solace in His loving embrace.

historical_references.reference: In medieval folklore, Thalassina was a sea nymph or mermaid associated with the Adriatic Sea. The name Thalassina comes from the Greek 'thalassa' meaning sea.
historical_references.context: Thalassina was believed to help sailors navigate the treacherous waters of the Adriatic Sea and protect them from storms and pirates.

historical_references.reference: According to Greek mythology, Thalassina was the daughter of Poseidon, the god of the sea, and Amphitrite, the goddess of the sea. She was one of the Nereids, sea nymphs who attended to Poseidon and the sea.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient Greece (8th century BC to 146 BC)
historical_references.context: Thalassina and the other Nereids were believed to have the power to control the sea and weather, and were often depicted as beautiful and graceful figures.
